Status

title: FOIA Request – M/I Homes Granby Yard Pre-Application Meeting and Related Communications

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: FOIA Request – M/I Homes Granby Yard Pre-Application Meeting and Related Communications
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act, 5 ILCS 140/1 et seq., I request copies of the following public records concerning the proposed M/I Homes “Granby Yard” development, an approximately 84-unit townhouse development proposed near Bluff Avenue and Cossitt Avenue in La Grange.

Based on public reporting, including reporting by La Grange Patch, Village Manager Jack Knight stated that a pre-application meeting between M/I Homes and Village officials occurred on July 21, 2026, concerning the concept plans for this development.

For purposes of this request, the project may also be identified in Village records by references to M/I Homes, Granby Yard, the proposed 84- or 85-unit townhouse development, the property or parcels southeast of Bluff and Cossitt Avenues, or other descriptions of the proposed development.

1. July 21, 2026 pre-application meeting

Please provide all existing records relating to the pre-application meeting held on or about July 21, 2026, including:

Any pre-application meeting summary, memorandum, staff report, meeting notes, minutes, agenda, agenda materials, or similar document;
Any staff notes or handwritten/electronic notes concerning the meeting;
Any attendee list, sign-in sheet, or record identifying Village officials, employees, consultants, representatives of M/I Homes, attorneys, engineers, architects, or other persons who participated;
Any presentation, site plan, concept plan, drawing, rendering, map, development proposal, or other materials presented or discussed at the meeting;
Any comments, recommendations, questions, concerns, or requests for additional information communicated by Village officials or staff concerning the proposed development;
Any follow-up memorandum, correspondence, or other record generated as a result of the meeting; and
Any records reflecting the date, time, location, scheduling, or purpose of the pre-application meeting.

2. Communications between M/I Homes and the Village before the pre-application meeting

Please provide copies of all emails and email attachments exchanged between M/I Homes (including M/I Homes of Chicago, LLC, and any M/I Homes representative, employee, attorney, engineer, architect, consultant, or other representative acting on its behalf) and any Village of La Grange employee, official, consultant, or representative using a @lagrangeil.gov email address concerning the proposed Granby Yard development or the proposed townhouse development near Bluff and Cossitt Avenues during the period:

April 21, 2026 through July 21, 2026.

This portion of the request is specifically limited to communications concerning the proposed development, including but not limited to:

Granby Yard;
M/I Homes;
the proposed 84- or 85-unit townhouse development;
Bluff Avenue;
Cossitt Avenue;
the Indiana Harbor Belt Railroad-adjacent property;
concept plans or preliminary plans;
the pre-application meeting;
zoning, land use, planned development, special-use, subdivision, density, parking, traffic, stormwater, engineering, environmental, demolition, or site-development issues associated with the proposal; and
scheduling or preparation for the July 21, 2026 pre-application meeting.

Please include both incoming and outgoing emails, including attachments and any email chains contained within responsive records.

3. Records concerning the project immediately following the pre-application meeting

Please also provide records created or received between July 21, 2026 and August 7, 2026 concerning the proposed Granby Yard development and the Village's review or discussion of the proposal, including emails, memoranda, meeting notes, staff comments, concept plans, and communications with M/I Homes or its representatives.

This latter date range is intended to capture the Village's contemporaneous records following the pre-application meeting and before the August 7, 2026 neighborhood-meeting notice reported publicly.

Search parameters

For the email portion of this request, please search the relevant Village email accounts for communications with M/I Homes and its representatives using reasonably apparent identifying terms, including:

“M/I Homes,” “M&I Homes,” “M I Homes,” “Granby Yard,” “84 units,” “85 units,” “townhomes,” “townhouses,” “Bluff,” “Cossitt,” and other readily apparent identifiers associated with this proposed development.

If the Village knows of a more specific project name, parcel number, development application number, or other identifier used internally for this proposal, please use that identifier as an additional search term.

I am requesting existing records only and am not asking the Village to create a new record, summary, or compilation.

If any portion of this request is considered overly broad, please identify the specific portion and the basis for that determination rather than treating the entire request as deficient. I am willing to reasonably narrow a particular search if necessary, but request that responsive portions of the request be processed independently.

If any responsive record contains information the Village believes is exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt material and produce the remainder of the record, citing the specific statutory exemption supporting each redaction pursuant to 5 ILCS 140/3(g).

Please provide the responsive records electronically, preferably in their native electronic format where practicable. For emails, please preserve the date, time, sender, recipients, subject line, and attachments.

Please advise me before incurring any fees beyond those permitted by the Illinois Freedom of Information Act.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Concerned Citizen of La Grange

title: LaVerne NASA

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

(1) Outgoing correspondence issued by the Office of the Associate Administrator for Space Flight, for the period January 1, 1986 through December 31, 1988, addressed to Albert A. LaVerne, M.D., of New York, New York, concerning photographs or photographic enlargements of the STS-51-L (Challenger) accident. Rear Admiral Richard H. Truly held that office for part of this period and is the reported signatory of at least one such letter, but that attribution reaches me secondhand and may be mistaken. I therefore ask that the search cover the office and not be limited to letters bearing his signature.

(2) Incoming correspondence from Albert A. LaVerne, M.D., together with its enclosures, routing slips, referral memoranda, and any entry in the Headquarters correspondence control or tracking system then in use, for the same period, held by the Office of the Associate Administrator for Space Flight or by the Headquarters correspondence control function.

(3) Records of Jay F. Honeycutt for the period January 1, 1986 through December 31, 1988, arising from his service in the Office of the Associate Administrator for Space Flight with responsibility for coordinating Presidential Commission and Congressional activities, that concern Albert A. LaVerne, photographic enlargements of the STS-51-L accident, or inquiries on that subject from the office of Senator Alfonse M. D'Amato.

(4) Records of the Office of the Administrator for the period January 1, 1987 through December 31, 1987 reflecting a request from the office of Senator Alfonse M. D'Amato for a meeting between Administrator James C. Fletcher and Albert A. LaVerne, including appointment and scheduling records, briefing or background memoranda prepared for that request, and any letter or memorandum declining it.

(5) Congressional correspondence files of the Office of Legislative Affairs for the period January 1, 1986 through December 31, 1988 concerning inquiries from the offices of Senator Alfonse M. D'Amato, Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan, or Senator Claiborne Pell relating to photographs or photographic enlargements of the STS-51-L accident, or to independent photographic analysis of that accident by persons outside the agency.

I am a writer researching how material of this kind moved through the agency and the Senate after the accident. I should say plainly that Dr. LaVerne's underlying claims were not credible and I am not advancing them. My interest is in the agency's handling, which is a documentable question in a way the claims themselves are not.

Records disposition. These records are approximately forty years old. If any responsive records have been transferred to the National Archives and Records Administration, I ask that your response identify the accession number and the applicable records disposition schedule, so that I may request them from NARA directly. I ask that a transfer of custody not be treated as the basis for a "no records" determination without that information.

Personal privacy. Albert A. LaVerne was born on January 17, 1916 and would now be 110 years old. Consistent with the presumption of death that agencies apply to individuals born more than 100 years ago, I ask that Exemption 6 not be treated as a bar to acknowledging or releasing these records. Independently of that, the records sought are the agency's own official correspondence on a matter of public concern, namely the cause of a fatal accident investigated by a Presidential Commission, and any residual privacy interest in the name of a correspondent is outweighed by the public interest in how the agency responded. If you nonetheless conclude that Exemption 6 applies to his identifying information, I ask that you release the records with that information redacted rather than withhold them in full, and that you release all reasonably segregable portions of any record withheld in part.

Search documentation. If you locate no responsive records, I ask that your response state which offices and record systems were searched, the search terms applied, and the date range used. A documented negative result is a useful outcome for me and I would prefer it to a bare statement that no records were found.

Referral and scope. The Kennedy Space Center aspects of this matter, namely the sale of photographic material to Dr. LaVerne and a telephone approach from a Kennedy Space Center employee to commercial photographic laboratories in Westchester County, New York, are the subject of a separate request directed to that Center and are not sought here. If Headquarters nonetheless holds records touching those aspects, I would welcome them. If responsive Headquarters records are in the custody of another NASA component, I ask that this request be referred to that component rather than closed.

Fees. I publish this research publicly and ask to be treated as a representative of the news media for fee purposes. To prevent any delay over fee category, I agree in advance to pay processing fees of up to $25 without further consultation, and ask to be contacted before any charge above that amount is incurred.

Exemptions. If any portion of this request is denied, please cite the specific exemption relied upon and provide a description of the withheld material sufficient to permit an administrative appeal.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

Your FOIA request is denied. In Illinois there are only three groups of people who may obtain child abuse and neglect records:


1. The subject of the report.

2. The representative of the subject of the report or a person authorized to get the reports on the subjects behalf.

3. Those individuals authorized access to records under the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act (325 ILCS 5/11.1).


By law, everyone else is specifically prohibited from viewing child protection investigation records. If specific case and investigation records exist, they may not be disclosed under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA).  DCFS is specifically prohibited by the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act (ANCRA) from releasing any information regarding reports of child abuse and neglect to anyone else. 325 ILCS 5/11. This statute is in place to protect the privacy of the children and families served by the Department.


DCFS child protection records are exempt records under the Freedom of Information Act and ANCRA. The following Illinois statutes and DCFS Rules prohibit the disclosure of the requested records:


 5 ILCS 140/7 (Illinois Freedom of Information Act) (Sec. 7. Exemptions. (1)(a) Information specifically prohibited from disclosure by federal or State law or rules and regulations implementing federal or State law.)


 325 ILCS 5/11 (Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act) ("All records concerning reports of child abuse and neglect or records concerning referrals under this Act and all records generated as a result of such reports or referrals, shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as specifically authorized by this Act or other applicable law.")


 Department Rule 431.40 (Confidentiality of Personal Information of Persons Served by the Department) ("Except as allowed in these rules, no personal information obtained concerning a person served by the Department or concerning the subjects of a child abuse or neglect report may be disclosed by the Department without the written consent of that individual...")


 Department Rule 431.20 (subject of a report) means any child reported to the child abuse/neglect State Central Register and his or her parent, personal guardian, or other person responsible for the child's welfare who is named in the report.


You have the right to have your request reviewed by the Public Access Counselor (PAC) at the Office of the Illinois Attorney General. 5 ILCS 140/9.5(a). You can file your request for review with the PAC at:
